worked_solution:
For the two lines to be perpendicular, their slopes must multiply to $-1.$

- The first line is in slope-intercept form, and the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So the slope of the line $y=7x-2$ is $7.$

- To find the slope of $kx-14y=7,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}kx-14y & =7 \\ 14y & =kx-7 \\ y & =\frac{k}{14}x-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the line $kx-14y=7$ is $\frac{k}{14}.$

Multiplying the slopes together, we have

$$
7\cdot (\frac{k}{14})=-1\,⟹\,k=-2.
$$
